cap: A pregnancy loss is named from two findings: whether the cervical os is open and whether tissue has passed. A threatened loss has a closed os and a live embryo, an inevitable loss has an open os, and a missed loss keeps a nonviable embryo behind a closed os. At least half of first-trimester losses are chromosomal, but after two or more losses, antiphospholipid syndrome, a septate uterus and parental translocations are looked for, and antiphospholipid syndrome is treated with low-dose aspirin plus heparin.
